summary: @qlik/oxfmt-config preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB bundle
details: The package advertises itself as a small shared oxfmt formatter config but its declared preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it to run a sibling file `math_init.js` (727 KB) at the tarball root. Both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are heavily obfuscated: setup.mjs uses obfuscator.io-style `_0xNNNNNN` identifiers with per-function key-remapping objects that hide identifiers such as `execFileSync`, `unzip`, `powershell`, and the Bun download URL; math_init.js is a Bun-compiled CJS bundle with a rotated string-array decoder (`WV8StW` shifter, ~1300-entry constants table, custom base64 alphabet). No hash or signature check is performed on the downloaded runtime, and `math_init.js` has no relationship to the package's declared purpose. If a `bun` binary is already present in PATH it is used to execute `math_init.js` directly. The alternate-runtime-dropper shape (execute an opaque bundle under a freshly-downloaded second language runtime) bypasses normal Node/npm inspection and is the canonical shape of an install-time supply-chain attack.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
